Neonatal Cubital fossa Median antecubital, cephalic and basilic veins - Median antecubital, cephalic and basilic veins are easy to hit and tend to last quite well if splinted properly.  These veins are the preferred sites for insertion of percutaneous central venous catheters.  These should be avoided unless absolutely necessary in any infant likely to need long term IV therapy. The median nerve and brachial artery are both in the same anatomical vicinity and therefore vulnerable to damage.
